name: Obadiah
overview: Obadiah was a male member of the tribe of Gad noted for being the second Gadite to join David at Ziklag. His arrival at David's side signifies early support during a critical period, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 12:9. This positions him among the faithful who aligned with David before his kingship was fully established.
namesAndTitles: The name Obadiah means 'servant [worshiper] of YHWH,' reflecting a personal identity devoted to the Lord. This proper name, as noted in 1 Chronicles 12:9, underscores his role as a faithful servant within God's people.
familyAndRelationships: Obadiah is explicitly identified as a descendant of Gad, linking him to one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Beyond this tribal affiliation, Scripture does not record additional family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Obadiah's significance lies in his early allegiance to David during a formative time at Ziklag, demonstrating loyalty to God's anointed leader. Being the second Gadite to join David suggests he was among the first from his tribe to support the future king, highlighting his role in the consolidation of David's followers. His tribal identity and timely commitment contribute to understanding the composition and unity of David's supporters.
